The database schema for the database rschema_0238 consists of 8 tables. The tables are described as follows:
1. The `class` table represents the classes or courses offered by the system. It has columns for `class_id` (a unique identifier for each class), `class_name` (the name of the class), `department_name` (the department offering the class), and `grade` (the grade level of the class). The primary key for this table is `class_id`.
2. The `member` table represents the members of the system. It has columns for `member_id` (a unique identifier for each member), `name` (the name of the member), `password` (the member's password), `email` (the member's email), `age` (the member's age), `work_unit` (the member's work unit), `phone_number` (the member's phone number), and `class_id` (a foreign key referencing the `class` table). The primary key for this table is `member_id`.
3. The `announcement` table represents the announcements made by the system. It has columns for `announcement_id` (a unique identifier for each announcement), `announcement_time` (the time the announcement was made), `announcement_content` (the content of the announcement), and `class_id` (a foreign key referencing the `class` table). The primary key for this table is `announcement_id`.
4. The `message` table represents the messages exchanged by members. It has columns for `message_id` (a unique identifier for each message), `sender_id` (the member_id of the sender), `receiver_id` (the member_id of the receiver), `message_content` (the content of the message), `send_time` (the time the message was sent), and `read_flag` (a flag indicating whether the message has been read). The primary key for this table is `message_id`.
5. The `log` table represents the logs of members. It has columns for `log_id` (a unique identifier for each log), `log_content` (the content of the log), `time` (the time the log was created), `mood` (the mood of the member at the time of the log), and `member_id` (a foreign key referencing the `member` table). The primary key for this table is `log_id`.
6. The `application` table represents the applications made by members. It has columns for `application_id` (a unique identifier for each application), `application_time` (the time the application was made), `approval_flag` (a flag indicating whether the application has been approved), `application_content` (the content of the application), and `member_id` (a foreign key referencing the `member` table). The primary key for this table is `application_id`.
7. The `member_message` table represents the messages received by members. It has columns for `member_id` (a foreign key referencing the `member` table), `message_id` (a foreign key referencing the `message` table), and `message_count` (the number of messages received by the member). The primary key for this table is a composite of `message_id` and `member_id`.
8. The `member_sent_message` table represents the messages sent by members. It has columns for `sender_id` (a foreign key referencing the `member` table), `receiver_id` (a foreign key referencing the `member` table), `message_content` (the content of the message), `send_time` (the time the message was sent), and `read_flag` (a flag indicating whether the message has been read). The primary key for this table is a composite of `sender_id`, `receiver_id`, and `send_time`.
All tables allow null values except for the `NOT NULL` constraints, and all columns have the appropriate data types for their domains. The tables are set up to maintain referential integrity, with foreign keys referencing the primary keys of other tables. The `ON DELETE CASCADE` and `ON UPDATE CASCADE` options are used to automatically delete or update the corresponding records in the referenced table when the record in the referencing table is deleted or updated.
gold_question:
This is a Student Information Management System. The main functions of the system are as follows:
1.Student Information Management: Manages basic student information such as student ID, name, gender, school, department, major, and ID number.
2.Teacher Information Management: Manages teacher information, including teacher ID, name, gender, title, and contact number.
3.Course Information Management: Manages course details, including course name, hours, credits, etc.
4.Grade Management: Stores students’ performance data, including regular grades, experimental grades, mid-term grades, and final grades.
5.Permission Management: Manages student and administrator permissions, including user ID, username, password, and role.
Each teacher can teach multiple courses, and each course can be taught by multiple teachers.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0238
CREATE TABLE `class` (
  `class_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `class_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `department_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `grade` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`class_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `member` (
  `member_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `age` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `work_unit` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `phone_number` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  `class_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`member_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `member_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`class_id`) REFERENCES `class` (`class_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `announcement` (
  `announcement_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `announcement_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `announcement_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `class_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`announcement_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `announcement_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`class_id`) REFERENCES `class` (`class_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `message` (
  `message_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `sender_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `receiver_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `message_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `send_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `read_flag` tinyint(1) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`message_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `log` (
  `log_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `log_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `mood` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `member_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`log_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `log_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`member_id`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `application` (
  `application_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `application_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `approval_flag` tinyint(1) DEFAULT NULL,
  `application_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `member_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`application_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `application_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`member_id`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `member_message` (
  `member_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `message_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `message_count` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`message_id`, `member_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `member_message_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`member_id`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `member_message_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`message_id`) REFERENCES `message` (`message_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `member_sent_message` (
  `sender_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `receiver_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `message_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `send_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `read_flag` tinyint(1) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`sender_id`, `receiver_id`, `send_time`),
  CONSTRAINT `member_sent_message_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`sender_id`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `member_sent_message_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`receiver_id`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
